feat-convert-insightsbookingservice-to-u.head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
feat-convert-insightsbookingservice-to-u.prTitle: feat: convert InsightsBookingService to use Prisma.sql raw queries

comentarios.texto: The caching sentinel logic in the service is now completely untested, so a regression that rebuilds conditions on every call or returns stale conditions can ship without any test failing. Re-add the caching tests using the new `Prisma.sql` expectations (first call builds the condition, second call returns an equal value), mirroring the routing service suite.

When a caller embeds the result as `WHERE ${base} AND <extra>`, SQL operator precedence turns it into `A OR (B AND extra)`, which can leak rows outside the authorization scope or ignore the extra predicate. Always wrap the fragment `getBaseConditions` returns in parentheses, using `Prisma.sql` for `authConditions` and `filterConditions`, and wrap the eventTypeId OR-fragment in its own parentheses.

The signature advertises that status sync participates in source-based cycle prevention, but the guard is never applied, so an inbound status webhook from integration A can still produce outbound status updates that loop exactly as the assignee case did. Either remove the unused parameter or thread `assignment_source` through the `sync_status_outbound` task into `should_sync("outbound_status", assignment_source)`.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.prTitle: feat(uptime): Add ability to use queues to manage parallelism

comentarios.texto: Because the tracker supports sparse offsets, this loop costs CPU proportional to the numeric span `max_offset - start` rather than the number of tracked offsets, so a single large gap burns CPU on every ~1s commit cycle. Iterate the sorted set of tracked offsets instead, walking `sorted(o for o in all_offsets if o >= start)` and stopping at the first offset that is missing contiguously or still outstanding.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.prTitle: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding

comentarios.texto: Administrators cannot add or edit embedding relationships for legitimate hosts such as `example.technology` because the new validation rejects suffixes longer than five letters, even though the previous hostname comparison supported them. Remove the five-letter suffix restriction or use a hostname validator that supports current domain suffixes.

`ensure_loaded!` is only defined on the `FallbackLocaleList` instance that config/initializers/i18n.rb assigns to `I18n.fallbacks`, so any environment where that initializer has not populated `I18n.fallbacks` with a `FallbackLocaleList` (the initializer file failing to load before `set_locale` runs, a reload in dev/test/console, or Rails reassigning `I18n.fallbacks`) raises `NoMethodError` on every request. Guard the call with `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! if I18n.fallbacks.respond_to?(:ensure_loaded!)`, or move the preload into the backend itself so it does not depend on a specific `I18n.fallbacks` type.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.prTitle: fix: handle collective multiple host on destinationCalendar

comentarios.texto: When no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` receives an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link never reaches the description. Compute `calendarId` once as `selectedCalendar || "primary"` and use it in both the insert and the patch call.

OAuth2 and GitHub require the exchange `redirect_uri` to be identical to the authorize value, so omitting it makes GitHub return `redirect_uri_mismatch` with no `access_token` and the pipeline shows the generic failure page for every installation. Add `"redirect_uri": redirect_uri` to `data`, matching `OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params` (oauth2.py:273-280).

When the frontend sends `installation_id=null` (as GitHub's user-account install flow does), the literal string `"null"` passes the `is None` check, is bound as state, and is later passed to `Integration.objects.get(external_id="null")`, which always misses and routes the user to the generic "Invalid installation request." page instead of redirecting to the app installer. Treat falsy and `"null"` values as absent, e.g. `if not installation_id or installation_id == "null": return self.redirect(self.get_app_url())`.

implement-recovery-key-support-for-user-.head: ce2dcc537b4b1f98a335e88cfe8e0b804483252a
implement-recovery-key-support-for-user-.prTitle: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers

comentarios.texto: Because `getMyUser` returns null when the username is missing from the `users` map, accessing `myUser.recoveryCodes` throws a `NullPointerException` on every `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` call, including the new `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` used during login. Return `Stream.empty()` when `myUser` is null, matching the existing guard in methods like `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.head: eb9623b4e787303a3bd15e10bbbdb78d59875ac6
optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.prTitle: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert

comentarios.texto: `span_count` receives the cardinality of the destination key `set_key` after the union, not the size of `span_key`/`parent_key` being merged, so when `set_key` already holds spans from an earlier insert (the common case for an in-progress segment) it counts those pre-existing spans and `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` evicts far more than the intended overflow, silently discarding valid recent and root spans. Derive the count from the merged key itself, e.g. `span_count = redis.call("zcard", set_key)` after the unions (or subtract the prior `zcard(set_key)` from the `zunionstore` result) before deciding how many to pop.

`_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (line 578), not on `PRCommentWorkflow`, so this static reference raises `AttributeError` whenever the helper runs and breaks the title-truncation feature entirely. Reference `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)`, or move `_truncate_title` next to the workflow helpers.

Any write events arriving between the search watcher starting and `initWatcher` subscribing are consumed by the search reader but never reach the broadcaster, so Watch subscribers silently miss those changes. Subscribe the broadcaster by calling `initWatcher` before starting the search event-draining goroutine, or have both consume from a single shared event source.
